item.title: Detroit Pistons Announce Concerning Duncan Robinson Injury Update
item.description: The Detroit Pistons have received some concerning injury news during Saturday night’s matchup against the Miami Heat, and it involves one of their most productive offensive players. According to the team’s official public relations account , Duncan Robinson is questionable to return due to left thigh soreness . Robinson exited the first half with 4:17 remaining and did not return to begin the second half. Omari Sankofa II of the Detroit Free Press initially noted Robinson’s absence after halftime, reporting that the veteran sharpshooter had not returned to the floor. Shortly afterward, the Pistons confirmed the injury designation, leaving his availability for the remainder of the game uncertain. Nov 12, 2026; Washington, District of Columbia, USA; Detroit Pistons forward Duncan Robinson (55) celebrates with Pistons guard Ausar Thompson (9) and Pistons guard Cade Cunningham (2) after making a go-ahead three point field goal against the Washington Wizards during the second overtime at Capital One Arena. Mandatory Credit: Geoff Burke-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Duncan Robinson Injury Adds to Pistons’ Concerns The potential loss of Robinson would be another frustrating development for a Detroit team already dealing with significant injuries. Starting center Jalen Duren remains sidelined with a right hamstring strain, while guard Isaiah Joe was also ruled out of Saturday’s game with a right hip contusion, according to the NBA’s official injury report . Robinson has been one of Detroit’s most valuable offensive contributors early in the 2026-27 season, providing much-needed perimeter shooting alongside Cade Cunningham. His impressive start has already created an interesting contract decision for the Pistons , who must decide whether to fully guarantee his salary later this season. The 32-year-old entered the season with plenty to prove and has responded by becoming a major piece of Detroit’s offense. His ability to stretch the floor has been especially important with Duren unavailable and head coach J.B. Bickerstaff adjusting his rotations. Detroit recently moved Daniss Jenkins into the starting lineup , giving the Pistons another offensive contributor alongside Cunningham and Robinson. If Robinson cannot return, Detroit will need additional production from its remaining perimeter players. For now, the Pistons have not announced that Robinson is officially out for the remainder of Saturday’s game. The team will continue evaluating his status, and additional information regarding the severity of his thigh soreness has not been released.

item.title: Fiji 'did Ireland a favour' before South Africa game
item.description: Fiji boss Jake White (left) believes Andy Farrell (right) and Ireland must improve before facing South Africa [Getty Images] Former South Africa head coach Jake White said his Fiji side "did Ireland a favour" in Saturday's Nations Championship contest before the Irish face the Springboks in Dublin next week. Fiji lost 43-15 to Ireland at Aviva Stadium having frustrated Andy Farrell's side during a closely contested first half. While Ireland scored 26 unanswered points in the second half, White - who led South Africa to World Cup glory in 2007 - said Andy Farrell's team cannot afford similarly sluggish spells against the back-to-back world champions. "We were playing a little bit like South Africa to be honest, I think that sums it up," said the 62-year-old. "We were letting Ireland have the ball and we were happy to defend against them and we were happy for them to try to outwork us." Asked to assess Ireland and South Africa's highly-anticipated meeting on Saturday (16:40 GMT), White added: "Well, I think we probably did Ireland a favour today. "Let me put it that way, because I think Ireland deep down know that if they play like that against South Africa, they're gonna be up against it." Ireland shake off sluggish start to brush aside Fiji White, who was appointed Fiji boss last month, was frustrated that his side opted to take a tap penalty instead of a scrum when the game was in the balance in the second half. "I know how South Africa operate and they would've taken that scrum there, they would have backed the fact that they wanted to get [Ireland] a yellow card," said White. "They would have taken another scrum and another scrum and another scrum, and they wouldn't have worried about the ref making a call about collapsing or early engaging. "The five-metre line-outs that we didn't take opportunities in, and the five-metre scrum and tap penalties, South Africa will turn those into points and I'm sure that Andy [Farrell] and the players will be aware of that. "They [Ireland] have been around a long time, and they know what's coming, and that's probably why he picked the team that he did because he wanted to make sure that they get a little bit more gun-ready for next weekend, because the easiest thing would have been to change the team and then they're probably one game shy of playing South Africa next week." White added: "If I'm coaching South Africa and Malcolm Marx is standing there [as captain], there's no way he is going to say, 'we'll take the tap'. There's no way that happens. "Malcolm Marx will say, 'let's take the scrum,' or 'we'll kick it out into the corner and we'll take the line-out'. And that's because they back themselves in those situations." When White's comments were put to Farrell, the Ireland boss said: "We were just saying in the changing rooms that we learned some good lessons and we'll use them in the right manner for next week." item.description: MIAMI, FLORIDA - NOVEMBER 14: Christian Pulisic #10 of United States celebrates scoring his team's third goal with teammates during the CONCACAF Nations League Quarterfinal match between Haiti and United States at Nu Stadium on November 14, 2026 in Miami, Florida. (Photo by JC Ruiz/Getty Images) | Getty Images In their first competitive match since their World Cup loss to Belgium, and their penultimate match under Mauricio Pochettino, the US soundly handled Haiti in Nations League play by a final score of 6-0. The match started out more slowly than the final score would indicate with the US tallying just once in the opening half, the goal coming on an Auston Trusty header off a Sebastian Berhalter free kick in the 10th minute. Diego Kochen had to make a big stop in the 15th minute to keep things level but the US would dominate possession and go into the half up 1-0. The US would come out flying in the second half with Julian Hall scoring his first goal in a competitive match for the USMNT, Christian Pulisic would score a brace, and Weston McKennie and Folarin Balogun would add to the tally as well. A second Haiti opportunity would be called back due to a narrow offsides, saving Kochen some embarrassment after coming out of his goal but failing to clear, and the match would finish 6-0. It was an eventful match and included first time caps for goal scorer Julian Hall as well as Justin Hall, Adri Mehmeti, and Mathis Albert who would come in as second half substitutes. Thanks to the result, the US will go into the second leg of their Nations League quarter-final matchup needing simply to not loose by six goals in Mauricio Pochettino’s final match to move on to the semi-finals next March. There were a number of goal scorers, and a clean sheet, but rather than giving you our man of the match we want you to have a voice. item.title: St. Mary's water polo falls short to Rio Americano in CIF SJS final
item.description: It was simply one of those days. St. Mary's girls water polo had no shortage of opportunities . Shots glanced off the crossbar. Chances inside 2 meters disappeared before a shot could be taken. Even wide-open looks in front of the goal failed to find the net. Unfortunately for the Rams, it came at the worst possible time . In Saturday's CIF Sac-Joaquin Section Division II championship game, No. 1 St. Mary's suffered its second straight loss in the section final , falling 8-4 to No. 2 Rio Americano, the Capital Valley Conference champion, at North Natomas Aquatic Complex on Nov. 14. "It felt like every time we had the perfect opportunity, we just missed the mark," Loyola Marymount commit Reyna Biedermann said. "Even when we made a cutoff and had a chance to go on offense, somehow they kept the ball. Things just didn't go our way." The TCAL champion entered averaging nearly 14 goals per game but managed just four, its second-lowest total of the season. Reyna, Denali Elliott, Gemma Lichter and Ella Fernandez were the Rams' goal scorers. "I get choked up just trying to describe this group," St. Mary's coach Vanessa Vincent said. "We've worked so hard for so long to get here. We didn't get to lift our first banner, but regardless of the outcome, I couldn't be more proud." Rio Americano, meanwhile, got two goals from Hannah Holladay and one apiece from six other players. "We believe that everybody's a participant on our team, and everybody practices hard," Rio Americano coach Rachel Ruano said. "It's nice that they can step into those big moments." 'Just didn't go in' The start was promising. Rio Americano took an early 1-0 lead on Alexa Kronbetter's goal, but St. Mary's responded. Reyna converted from 5 meters, and Emery Biedermann found Elliott on a step-out play. Then the scoring stopped. For St. Mary's, the drought stretched all the way to the 3:47 mark of the fourth quarter. "We could've made those adjustments earlier," Vincent said. "We eventually did, but the shots just weren't falling. Their goalie was reading us really well, and they pressured us hard. We were taking good shots. They just didn't go in." It began with 10 seconds left in the first quarter. Claire McGrath and Erin Ash had just put Rio Americano ahead 3-2 when Reyna sent a lob shot off the crossbar. The second quarter brought more of the same, only worse. Hannah Holladay scored from outside, while Reyna and Emery each missed a 5-meter attempt. St. Mary's then had a one-on-one shot from 2 meters blocked before another attempt during a 6-on-5 advantage was saved, sending the Rams into halftime down 4-2. "Everybody played great," Ruano said. "It was really fun seeing our bench come in and score a couple of goals." And the third quarter wasn't much different. item.title: MARQUETTE VOLLEYBALL WINS THE 2026 BIG EAST REGULAR SEASON TITLE!
item.description: THE CHAMPS ARE HERE | Credit: Marquette University In August, I led off the Three Questions part of the Marquette volleyball season preview with “Who’s doing what around here, anyway?” as the first question. Pretty much everything was up for grabs in Tom Mendoza’s second season in charge, although it seemed pretty likely that 2025 MAC Player of the Year Carson Tyler would have at least a decently sized role. Along the way, Kiera Schmidt went from the most reliable returning player on the roster to appearing in just 19 of 26 matches and just 49 of 97 sets. Emma Parks was the only returning outside hitting option of note, and she only logged 70 sets in 23 matches, ultimately only starting twice for the Golden Eagles, which is actually less than Schmidt started. Even the most likely answers to the questions in front of Mendoza ended up being anything but reliable as the season went along. And yet. On Saturday, Emma Parks was the one dropping the kills for the last three points of Marquette’s 3-0 (25-15, 25-22, 25-23) sweep of St. John’s that moved the Golden Eagles to 14-2 in Big East play. With the win, Marquette has clinched at least a share of the 2026 Big East regular season title, which is the fifth Big East title in program history. If Creighton wins, it’s a tie for the title and the Bluejays are the #1 seed. If the Wildcats prevail, they will play the role of spoiler since they’re already eliminated from the conference tournament and thus MU will be the outright champs and #1 seed. It was a two match homestand to end the year, and before getting to the Red Storm on Saturday, Marquette had to beat Seton Hall on Friday to set themselves up with a chance to clinch the title. MU did this with not a whole lot of difficulty, sweeping the Pirates with scores of 25-11, 25-21, and 25-16. The first set was over quickly with Marquette jumping out to a 15-5 lead right away. item.description: Nov 14, 2026; East Lansing, Michigan, USA; Washington Huskies quarterback Demond Williams Jr. (1) hands off the ball to Washington Huskies running back Jayden Limar (17) during the first quarter against the Michigan State Spartans at … | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Kate Pearson Halyburton, Editor Big Plays Early and Late Fuel Husky Win at Michigan State. Washington’s eight-play, 78-yard touchdown drive broke a 14-14 tie late in the fourth quarter at Michigan State. Running back Jayden Limar scored what was ultimately the game-winning touchdown to cap a possession that was fueled by explosive plays. Entering that drive, Washington had just one play of 10-plus yards in the second half. All four of its previous second-half possessions ended with a punt and combined for just 41 total yards. The game-winning touchdown drive featured four plays of 10-plus and gave Washington a 21-14 win at Michigan State. Big Plays Fuel Husky Win at Michigan State Explosive Passing Early Demond Williams started the game four for four passing with each throw traveling less than 10 air yards. His next two attempts then traveled 40-plus air yards each but were both overthrown, despite the receivers gaining a step on the defenders. That didn’t prevent Williams from continuing to attack the deep part of the field. Two plays after his deep incompletions, Williams connected with Chris Lawson for a 58-yard touchdown, hitting his receiver in stride as he was tackled across the goal line. It was Lawson’s first reception of 50-plus on the year, and it tied the football game at seven. On the Huskies’ next offensive possession, explosive plays again fueled the drive. Consecutive false start penalties turned a second and one into a second and 11, and Williams immediately responded to the adversity with three-straight explosive throws. He connected with Rashid Williams on a 26-yard sideline pass on the next play. The Husky receiver displayed excellent sideline awareness as he toe-tapped the green grass for a big-play first down. Williams targeted Decker DeGraaf for 33 yards on the next snap, before finding Lawson for a 17-yard touchdown, his second of the game. Lawson finished with 125 receiving yards on five catches (24.8 yards per reception) in what was his third 100-yard game in the last four outings. item.title: Kentucky falls to Florida: 3 things to know and postgame banter
item.description: The Kentucky Wildcats fell to the Florida Gators in Lexington on Saturday night by a final score of 21-14. The Cats came out ready to roll. They forced a Gator punt and then drove down the field on a 15-play, 86-yard drive for the game’s first score. Unfortunately, things slowed down tremendously after that. To make matters worse, the offense didn’t make the defense’s job any easier. After an egregious holding call in the end zone, Florida added two points on a safety, leading to a 7-2 UK lead at halftime. After the break, Kentucky did not come out as ready as you would expect. Kenny Minchey was sacked and fumbled the ball back to Florida on the opening drive of the second half. Florida was able to punch it in, but they decided to try an onside kick on the ensuing kickoff, which flipped all momentum back to the Cats after they recovered it. Kentucky answered with a score of its own to retake the lead 14-10. Once again, however, the Gators were able to consistently move the ball when Kentucky was not able to do the same. A field goal cut the lead to 14-13, and another touchdown extended the Gator lead to seven. Kentucky’s offense couldn’t answer, getting turned over on downs in back-to-back drives, and that was that. A special season has been flipped on its head. Two really disappointing games following an incredible run to start the season. That’s why we play the games. Florida isn’t a good football team, but Jon Sumrall showed why the Gators picked him in this one. Next up, the Cats will travel to CoMo to take on the Missouri Tigers next Saturday night. Two more games to finish out the season, albeit with less to play for coming into this game. The offense has been abysmal Will Stein is widely known as an impressive play-caller, but whether it’s him or Joe Sloan (more likely), the offense has been pretty disappointing for a while now. After scoring just six points on two field goals last week in an embarrassing performance against the Tennessee Volunteers, the Cats struggled for the majority of the night in this one. The offense is somewhat gimmicky. It’s been lacking explosiveness, and when the run game is nonexistent, like it was in this game, Kentucky struggles to get consistent results. The offense doesn’t lack creativity, but it requires execution each time out, along with playmakers that can make some guys miss, which UK simply lacks. Additionally, Minchey is, generally, pretty good at executing the offense, but when it breaks down, or it isn’t working, he really doesn’t do a good job improvising. item.description: The Red Wings are finally headed home and they'll be a happy bunch for several reasons. They've been away for eight days — four games — capping off a road-heavy part of the schedule the last several weeks. The Wings were also in the midst of a five-game losing streak and lost six of seven games. But the Wings are returning home with some momentum, after defeating Tampa Bay, 2-0, on Saturday, Nov. 14. item.description: Cypress Ranch will take on Allen at the UIL state championships. The Mustangs (40-7), who have won 29 consecutive matches, will face Allen (42-2) for the UIL Class 6A Division I title at 6 p.m. next Saturday at the Curtis Culwell Center in Garland. Lake Travis swept Cy Ranch in their first meeting at the Leander Volleypolooza tournament in August, and it looked like the rematch might be headed in the same direction. But the Mustangs, led by coach Collea McKinney, were able to swing the momentum back in their favor and win three consecutive sets to clinch their spot in the final. Regional champions for a second consecutive season, Cy Ranch will face an Allen team that is riding a 20-match winning streak of its own. The Eagles will be making their first state championship appearance since 2003 after sweeping Duncanville in the other semifinal match Saturday at the Thomas Coliseum in Haltom City. Cy Ranch is one of two Houston-area teams headed to state. The other is Lake Creek, which earned its spot in the Class 5A Division II final with a 25-20, 25-14, 25-20 win over New Braunfels at the Merrell Center in Katy. The Lions (43-10) have won 10 consecutive matches and will also be making their first championship match appearance. Lake Creek reached the semifinals in 2022 before losing to eventual champion Colleyville Heritage. Lake Creek, led by coach Kayli Kane, has swept four of its five playoff opponents and will play Abilene Wylie (39-4) for the state title at 11 a.m. next Saturday in Garland. item.description: The Detroit Lions are ready to bring some Honolulu Blue to Germany, and now we know exactly what they’ll be wearing when they take the field against the New England Patriots. Ahead of Sunday’s Week 10 matchup in Munich, the Lions revealed their uniform combination, opting for their traditional Honolulu Blue jerseys, silver pants, and silver helmets . The look was featured in a team graphic highlighting wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown, whose German heritage has made this international matchup particularly meaningful. The uniform combination also includes Honolulu Blue socks, giving Detroit a familiar look for its first international regular-season game since 2015. According to NBC Sports’ Week 10 uniform breakdown , the Patriots will counter with silver helmets, white jerseys, and silver pants. Detroit Lions Ready to Represent in Germany The Lions enter Sunday’s game with a 6-2 record and a four-game winning streak following their 19-9 victory over the Miami Dolphins. New England comes into the matchup at 5-4 after suffering a 45-27 loss to the Green Bay Packers. Detroit will serve as the designated home team at Munich’s Allianz Arena, and head coach Dan Campbell has already made it clear that he expects plenty of support. Campbell recently declared the Lions “Germany’s team” , pointing to the growing international fan base and St. Brown’s connection to the country. Lions owner Sheila Ford Hamp also predicted a blue wave of Detroit supporters in Munich, even taking a playful shot at the lack of Patriots fans she had encountered during the festivities. According to the Lions’ official game-day information , Sunday’s matchup will kick off at 9:30 a.m. ET on FOX , which is 3:30 p.m. local time in Germany. Detroit will be looking for its fifth consecutive victory while giving its international supporters something to celebrate. item.title: High school football: Rich cruises to fourth straight 1A 8-player state championship
item.description: The Rich Rebels celebrate with their trophy after winning against the Milford Tigers during a 1A 8-player state championship held at Eccles Coliseum in Cedar City on Saturday, Nov. 14, 2026. | Tess Crowley, Deseret News Rich’s dynasty in 8-player football doesn’t show any signs of slowing down. In a rematch of last year’s title game, top-seed Rich rolled past No. 2 seed Milford 69-35 at Southern Utah University on Saturday evening to claim its fourth straight 1A 8-player state championship. “It’s really surreal. It’s an awesome experience. Words can’t describe it,” said Rich senior Wilkes Weston, who had a monster performance Saturday with 194 rushing yards and three touchdowns. Rich beat Milford 65-19 in Week 2 this season, breaking the game open in the second half after leading by just seven at intermission. Three months later, Rich didn’t wait around in blowing the game open. Its offense scored every time it touched the ball but once the entire game, building a 35-14 halftime lead and coasting from there. “We believed we had an edge in this game, and I was grateful that the kids came and tried to take it rather than just be entitled to winning,” said Rich coach Tyson Larsen. “I felt like they came out and tried to take the victory and leave no doubt rather than just assume that because we beat them earlier in the year that it would happen again.” Weston set the tone on the first drive of the game, scoring on a 2-yard run, and after Milford tied the game 8-8 on the ensuing possession, Weston scored again on Rich’s second possession to stretch the lead to 14-8. Weston had high praise for his linemen after the game. “Those holes were massive for me to run through, so I could just keep on running all day long through those things,” Weston said. While Weston had a workhorse performance with 31 carries, fellow running backs Brady Cornia and Jasper Johnson benefited from those gaping holes with explosive plays. Cornia carried the ball five times for 124 yards and two touchdowns — including a 90-yard TD run — while Johnson ripped off two touchdowns and 90 rushing yards on just two carries. Already firmly in control at halftime, Cornia’s 90-yard run was the exclamation point for the Rebels. The former Los Angeles Lakers first-round pick scored a team-high 26 points Saturday in his NBA G League debut, shooting 8-of-13 from the field and 5-of-8 from the 3-point range in Westchester’s 104-95 loss to the Greensboro Swarm. Knecht added six rebounds, two assists and two steals. He was particularly sharp before halftime, making five of his seven attempts from beyond the arc. The Dalton Knecht Knicks debut provided an encouraging glimpse of the shooting ability that made him a first-round selection just two years ago. Dalton Knecht Shines Alongside Rookie Tyler Nickel Knecht provided Westchester with an immediate offensive threat in his first assignment with the New York Knicks’ G League affiliate. His five first-half 3-pointers highlighted an efficient scoring performance, although he didn’t make another shot from beyond the arc after halftime. View this post on Instagram Knecht finished with 26 points on just 13 field-goal attempts. He also collected four offensive rebounds, showing activity beyond his perimeter shooting. Tyler Nickel , New York’s second-round pick in the 2026 NBA draft, provided plenty of support. The former Vanderbilt standout scored 21 points on 8-of-15 shooting, including 5 of 8 from the 3-point range. The Knicks acquired Nickel’s draft rights after Phoenix selected him with the 47th overall pick in June. Together, Knecht and Nickel accounted for 47 of Westchester’s 95 points and 10 of its 16 3-pointers. Jaden Akins added 15 points and four assists, while Nick Jourdain contributed 12 points off the bench. A video of world number two Sabalenka angrily gesturing and swearing in Russian during her 6-3 3-6 6-1 defeat by Ukraine's Svitolina was posted on social media on Saturday. Some commentators interpreted Belarusian Sabalenka's comments as an insult towards Svitolina or Ukrainians in general. Sabalenka later wrote on social media that "my comment was not directed at Elina" but she lost her temper because of the behaviour of some fans. "I was frustrated with a small group of spectators who were aggressively cheering my mistakes, and I reacted emotionally in the moment," the 28-year-old wrote. "That said, I should have handled my frustration differently, and I apologise to anyone offended." Sabalenka said Svitolina had played a great match, adding that she wished her "all the best for the rest of the tournament". Ukrainian players have a long-standing policy of not shaking hands with Russian or Belarusian players because of the ongoing invasion of their country. item.title: Svitolina races into WTA Finals showpiece against Andreeva
item.description: Elina Svitolina is a three-time finalist at the WTA Finals [Getty Images] Elina Svitolina dropped just three games as she thrashed Linda Noskova to set up a WTA Finals showpiece against Mirra Andreeva. Ukraine's Svitolina was composed and aggressive in a 6-2 6-1 victory over Wimbledon champion Noskova in just 64 minutes. It caps a remarkable turnaround for world number six Svitolina in Indian Wells, having suffered a heavy defeat in her opening group match against Andreeva. However, she has shown all of her fighting spirit to win her next three matches, including snapping a six-match losing streak to Aryna Sabalenka on Friday. Svitolina now has 11 wins over top-10 opponents this year - the most of any player on the WTA Tour. "After losing the first match I was ready to go home, and now I'm in the final," the 32-year-old said. "I will do my homework with my coaches - I will try to win a bit more games than I did in the first match [against Andreeva]." Svitolina is back in the world's top 10 for the first time since October 2021. She took maternity leave in May 2022 to have daughter Skai, and has made an effort to play more aggressive tennis since her return. She returned brilliantly against Noskova, neutralising the Czech's big serve from the first game. Noskova was well below her best, hitting 11 double faults and committing 27 unforced errors to Svitolina's 18. It is the third time Svitolina has reached the final of the season-ending tournament, having lifted the trophy in 2018. Earlier, Andreeva became the youngest player for 22 years to reach the WTA Finals showpiece with a composed victory over Jessica Pegula. French Open champion Andreeva came back from a break down in both sets to win 6-3 6-4. The 19-year-old Russian is the youngest finalist at the season-ending event since Maria Sharapova, who was 17 when she won the title in 2004. Victory over American Pegula ensures Andreeva will finish the year as world number two. "I did not feel one bit of pressure today, I don't know why," Andreeva told Sky Sports. "Usually I feel like on these important points or when I have to close out the match or the set I get so tight. "But for some reason today I was just playing. I was just not thinking about anything, just trying to enjoy." Tournament debutant Andreeva has yet to drop a set and has not lost more than four games in any of her eight sets. The 18 games she has lost is the fewest for a finalist at the WTA Finals since the round-robin format was introduced in 2003. Under the guidance of coach Conchita Martinez, Andreeva has developed her serve into a real weapon. She won 77% of points behind her first serve and hit 17 winners to outmuscle Pegula. Andreeva also showed impressive composure, remaining unfazed despite going an early break down in both sets against the home favourite. item.description: AEW Full Gear 2026 Graphic All Elite Wrestling AEW has welcomed several notable former WWE stars in recent months, but Tony Khan and company had another surprise up their sleeves at Full Gear. This time, it was the arrival of the Kasper Brothers, formerly known as Julius and Brutus Creed in WWE. In the second match of AEW Full Gear’s main card, The Young Bucks defeated Mark Davis and Jake Doyle to retain the AEW World Tag Team Championship. The Motor City Machine Guns, the new No. 1 contenders after defeating FTR in a best-of-five series, came down to the ring to greet the champions, seemingly setting up their upcoming title match. However, an alarm sounded, and a logo for the “Kasper Brothers” appeared on the video screens inside the Mortgage Matchup Center. The moment left fans and even the wrestlers in the ring confused until the former Julius and Brutus Creed emerged on the stage. Previously known by those names in WWE, the brothers are now going by their real names, Jacob and Drew Kasper, respectively. They marched to the ring to confront the Motor City Machine Guns and The Young Bucks before FTR arrived and joined them in an attack on the babyfaces. It was one of AEW’s bigger surprise debuts in recent months. While Creed, Kingston and Dragunov were all notable additions, their arrivals had been heavily rumored before they officially debuted. Earlier this month, Fightful Select reported that the Kaspers had mutually agreed to leave WWE, where Jacob had been since 2020 and Drew since 2021. Both were collegiate wrestlers who transitioned to professional wrestling, beginning their careers in NXT before moving to WWE’s main roster in 2023. The Kasper Brothers were best known for their alliance with Ivy Nile and, later, Chad Gable as part of American Made. However, the group’s run together was relatively short-lived due to Gable’s absence with an injury. The brothers also played a role in the No Disqualification match between the two El Grande Americanos at Noche de Los Grandes in May. The Kaspers eventually returned to NXT in September, where they remained until their final match on Oct. 20 against Hank and Tank in the quarterfinals of the Dusty Rhodes Tag Team Classic. Their contracts expired shortly afterward, on Nov. 6. Long considered a tag team with potential, the Kaspers now have a chance to establish themselves in AEW’s red-hot tag team division alongside the likes of The Young Bucks, the Motor City Machine Guns, New Level and FTR. As one of the youngest duos in the division, they have plenty of room to grow in a new environment that could provide significant opportunities for both brothers. item.description: PITTSBURGH, PA - OCTOBER 11: Pat Freiermuth #88 of the Pittsburgh Steelers celebrates with Aaron Rodgers #8 after catching a 1 yard touchdown pass in the first half against the Indianapolis Colts at Acrisure Stadium on October 11, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. Aller/Getty Images) Getty The Pittsburgh Steelers enjoyed a much-needed bye week and are back in action Sunday night against the Cincinnati Bengals in a showdown for first place in the AFC North. This comes after the front office decided to avoid making any moves at the trade deadline. Specifically, plenty of fans were hoping to land a receiver or two to help Aaron Rodgers on offense. That did not happen and the team may already feel the effects of the inaction due to a key player hitting the injury report Saturday afternoon. Steelers Veteran Hits Injury Report The Steelers shared a post on X Saturday afternoon revealing tight end Pat Freiermuth is officially questionable for the Bengals game with an illness. It appears as if he will be a game-time decision depending on how he feels. This would be a big absence for the Steelers as Freiermuth leads the team in receiving touchdowns with four. His 25 receptions tie him for third on the team as well. The tight end has been a reliable option for Rodgers during a year when the wide receiver position has been hit with injuries and unexpected struggles. Michael Pittman Jr. and Roman Wilson are both on injured reserve, waiting to make their respective returns. Meanwhile, WR1 DK Metcalf is having a down year. This has left the likes of Freiermuth, Darnell Washington, and Jaylen Warren to help carry the load outside of the receiver position. That explains why fans on social media were vocal following Tuesday’s quiet trade deadline. A Battle for First Place Sunday’s game is a big one as the Steelers and Bengals both enter with identical 6-2 records. The Baltimore Ravens are without Lamar Jackson and the Cleveland Browns may be coming back down to Earth, leaving the Steelers and Bengals as the favorites to win the AFC North division. The two teams already squared off once this season back in Week 3, with the Steelers taking home a 30-27 victory. Rodgers and Joe Burrow threw three touchdowns apiece, but the difference in the game was Jaylen Warren breaking out and rushing for 127 yards. The absence of Freiermuth would loom large, putting more focus on Washington. However, he’s not exactly the easiest player to stop for any opposing defense. Freiermuth is sick, Pittman and Wilson remain on injured reserve, and the Steelers decided to keep the roster intact at the deadline.
